paper_title: Can LLMs Solve longer Math Word Problems Better
caption: (left) and (right) of scaling up SFT dataset across various model scales in the LLaMA-2 family. The results suggest scaling up model scales and SFT dataset can further improve .
model_annotation: This chart illustrates the CoLeG-R values (in percentage) for different LLaMA model variations and SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning) configurations. The horizontal axis displays the LLaMA model names, specifically "LLaMA-2-7B", "LLaMA-2-13B", and "LLaMA-2-70B", in that order from left to right. The vertical axis is labeled "CoLeG-R (%)" and ranges from 0 to 80, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The data is presented as grouped bars, with each model showing three bars representing different SFT configurations: "+ SFT on D₀" (pale blue), "+ SFT on D₀, D₁" (light pink), and "+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂" (medium pink-purple). Additionally, there is a single bar for "no SFT" (yellow-orange) for each model. The "no SFT" bars for "LLaMA-2-7B", "LLaMA-2-13B" and "LLaMA-2-70B" have approximate values of 22%, 25% and 27% respectively. The bars representing "+ SFT on D₀" generally have values between 65% and 72%. The pink-purple bars representing "+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂" tend to have the greatest values in each group, reaching a height of approximately 80% for "LLaMA-2-70B". A legend is provided to identify each of the four bar types. All bars are oriented vertically, and none appear to be visually emphasized beyond their color distinction.
